description: Train a sparse autoencoder on the tiny CPU Llama: a 16 -> 32 dictionary for layer 0's output, fitted to every token of the weekday prompts after BOS (`{'index': '1:'}`: position 0 is BOS, which SAE training leaves out, since on a trained model its stream is a massive-activation outlier). The tokens are harvested once, before the fit (`harvest.acts`, a ragged read), and the fit's body is the dictionary's `encode` of each minibatch's 2 prompts of them, so the model runs once in all. The objective is the dictionary's own scalars over what that encode saw: `reconstruction`, the mean squared error between each read vector and its decoding, plus 0.01 times `l1`, the mean absolute latent. Its decoder rows are kept at unit norm by a projection after each optimizer step. The trained dictionary is saved as a bundle (sae_train_ablation.json loads it) with each scalar's per-epoch history. The model is random, so its latents mean nothing; the mechanics are what this exercises.
